people.summary: Father of Gertrud Elise Becker (Christa's mother), so Thomas Kohlmann's maternal great-grandfather.
people.story: Father of Gertrud Elise Becker (Christa's mother), so Thomas Kohlmann's maternal great-grandfather. Kaufmann (merchant). Born 5 January 1875 in Herzberg, Kreis Schweinitz (Herzberg on the Black Elster), and died at home, Rothermundtstraße 5, Dresden, on 9 January 1938, aged 63, according to his civil death entry (Dresden V 1938 Nr. 52).[^anc-death-1938] The 2007 family chart has the two days the other way round (born 9 January, died 5 January); the record is preferred. The chart gives pneumonia as the cause.[^ahnentafel-2007] By 1903 he had his own shop: the Dresden address books of 1903 and 1905 list him as a merchant and owner of a grocery and drugstore (Kolonialwaren- und Drogenhandlung) on the ground floor of Ziegelstraße 2.[^slub-dresden-1903][^slub-dresden-1905] The family lived in the same house, and Gertrud was born there in January 1905; he reported her birth himself.[^anc-birth-1905] By 1926 the family lived at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Striesen, where he kept an ironmonger's shop on the ground floor ("Becker, R., Eisenwhdlg.").[^slub-dresden-1938] He was a witness at Gertrud's wedding to Alwin Eifler on 2 October 1926, aged 51.[^anc-marriage-1926] He was cremated at the Dresden crematorium in January 1938, certificate 60603.[^anc-cremation-1938] The chart records two sisters; a handwritten note names one as Marie (married surname perhaps Wettlitz) of Rothermundtstraße 5.

people.story: Mother of Gertrud Elise Becker (Christa's mother), so Thomas Kohlmann's maternal great-grandmother. Her civil death entry calls her Clara Elise Becker née Just, Hausfrau, born 1 December 1880 in Raun, Kreis Oelsnitz im Vogtland (birth registered at Bad Elster, Nr. 132).[^findbuch-death-1954] She married the merchant Richard Hermann Becker and lived in Dresden. Widowed in 1938, she later lived with her daughter's family at Wilthener Straße 19 in Bautzen, where she died at 2:10 in the morning of 27 December 1954, aged 74. Gertrud reported the death.[^findbuch-death-1954] The family chart says she was one of eight Just children (two sisters and five brothers) and died of heart failure.[^ahnentafel-2007]

people.summary: Father of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis.
people.story: Father of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis, and Thomas Kohlmann's maternal grandfather. Born on 7 October 1892 at half past three in the afternoon in the house Äußerst Mittelsohland Nr. 250, Sohland an der Spree, and baptised there on 16 October. He was the second child and first son of Ernst Gustav Eifler, a baker, and Johanna Christiane née Kahden.[^sohland-kb-1892] His marriage entry gives the same place.[^anc-marriage-1926] A Weickert & Eifler saddlery and upholstery shop already existed in Bautzen in 1921, run by the master saddler Bruno Weickert at Löbauer Straße 10.[^anc-bautzen-1921] In June 1922 the firm's steel-wire mattresses were on show at the opening of the Industriehof Gnaschwitz, a former munitions works south of Bautzen.[^bn-1922-06-26-industriehof] On 11 October 1922 Alwin, a Kaufmann (merchant), and Bruno Weickert founded the Stahldrahtmatratzenfabrik Weickert & Eifler as a partnership, entered in the Bautzen commercial register as Blatt 885, with premises at An den Fleischbänken 7.[^bn-1922-12-15-hr885] Three months later the partnership was dissolved: Bruno left, and from January 1923 Alwin carried on the business alone under the old name.[^bn-1923-01-26-hr885] That autumn the firm advertised abroad: "Oberlausitzer Stahldraht-Matratzen-Fabrik Weickert & Eifler, Bautzen. Export nach allen Ländern! Auslandsvertreter gesucht."[^ost-und-sued-1923] On 2 October 1926 Alwin, a "Fabrikant" living at Wendischer Graben 3 in Bautzen, married Gertrud Elise Becker at the Dresden V registry office (1926 Nr. 352). The witnesses were Ernst Eifler, a farmer of Sohland an der Spree Nr. 247, aged 61 (probably his father), and the bride's father.[^anc-marriage-1926] From 1928 he is listed as sole owner (Inhaber) of the Stahldrahtmatratzenfabrik Weickert & Eifler, with the factory at Gnaschwitz and his home and office at Neusalzaer Straße 38.[^slub-bautzen-1928] By 1935 the firm was at Martin-Mutschmann-Straße 19 (today Wilthener Straße 19), a house he owned by 1938.[^anc-bautzen-1935][^slub-bautzen-1938] The family chart says he died on 18 December 1968 of a basal skull fracture after a car accident, aged 76, and names his siblings as Max, Alfred and Martha.[^ahnentafel-2007] A note stamped on his 1926 marriage entry in Dresden on 6 November 1969 says he died on 18 December 1968 and that the death was registered at Zittau, about 30 km south east of Bautzen.[^anc-marriage-1926] That is why it is not in the Bautzen city register for 1968; Gertrud is recorded as widowed in 1973.[^findbuch-index-1968][^findbuch-death-1973] See the Weickert & Eifler page for the full story of the firm.

people.story: Mother of Christa Kohlmann and Sigrid Michaelis, and Thomas Kohlmann's maternal grandmother. Born 22 January 1905 at Ziegelstraße 2 in Dresden, daughter of the merchant Richard Hermann Becker, who reported the birth (Dresden I 1905 Nr. 165).[^anc-birth-1905] Living with her parents at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden-Striesen, she married Alwin Eifler on 2 October 1926 at the Dresden V registry office, aged 21.[^anc-marriage-1926] A Weickert & Eifler invoice of 9 April 1943 carries her signed receipt: "Betrag dankend erhalten. Gertrud Eifler. d. 28.4.1943." That shows she signed for the firm; whether she kept its books is not recorded.[^weickert-invoice-1943] In 1954 she reported her mother's death at the family house, Wilthener Straße 19, Bautzen.[^findbuch-death-1954] She died there, a widow, at 3:00 in the morning of 11 December 1973, aged 68 (Bautzen 1973 Nr. 1052).[^findbuch-death-1973] The family chart gives cancer as the cause.[^ahnentafel-2007]

people.story: Thomas's father, Herbert Kohlmann. The family gives his name in English as Herbert Coleman.[^family-correction-2026-11-26] He married Elise Christa Eifler, daughter of Alwin and Gertrud Eifler of the Bautzen mattress firm Weickert & Eifler, on 24 July 1952 in Bautzen; the date is on the 2007 family chart.[^ahnentafel-2007] They had three children, Thomas, Matthias and Sabine. Deceased. Earlier versions of this site gave his first name wrongly, a mix-up with Christa's father, Alwin Eifler, and the family corrected it on 26 November 2026. Herbert's birth, death, occupation and parents are not yet known. The Bautzen marriage entry of 1952 would name his parents, his birthplace and his occupation. Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a Bautzen butcher born in 1883, is a possible candidate for his father because of the surname, the town and his age, but nothing links them.

people.disambiguator: baker, later farmer, Sohland an der Spree
people.summary: Alwin Eifler's father, so Thomas Kohlmann's great-grandfather. A baker in Mittelsohland in 1890 and 1892, and probably the farmer Ernst Eifler of Sohland Nr. 247 who was a witness at Alwin's wedding in 1926.
people.story: Ernst Gustav Eifler was Alwin Eifler's father. The Sohland church book names him at the baptisms of his first two children: Martha Maria, born on 10 February 1890, and Ernst Alwin, born on 7 October 1892. Both were born in the house Äußerst Mittelsohland Nr. 250, where he lived as an Inwohner (a tenant, not an owner) and worked as a baker (Bäcker). His wife was Johanna Christiane Kahden of Mittelsohland.[^sohland-kb-1892][^sohland-kb-1890] Among the godparents was the wife of an Eifler from Niedercunnersdorf near Herrnhut, so the family probably had relatives there. Others were a bookbinder from Neugersdorf and a weaver from Wehrsdorf.[^sohland-kb-1892][^sohland-kb-1890] On 2 October 1926 a farmer named Ernst Eifler, of Sohland an der Spree Nr. 247, aged 61, signed as a witness at Alwin's wedding in Dresden.[^anc-marriage-1926] That is almost certainly the same man, by then farming a smallholding a few houses away. The 2007 family chart names Alwin's brothers Max and Alfred and his sister Martha.[^ahnentafel-2007] Martha is now proven by the church book; Max and Alfred are drawn as his sons too, with dashed lines until a record confirms them.

people.disambiguator: a lead for Herbert Kohlmann's family
people.summary: Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a butcher, was born on 21 September 1883 at Kötzschau near Lawalde (Kreis Löbau) and died in Bautzen on 27 February 1972, still living at Schäfferstraße 6, his address since 1925. He married Marie Ida Jurack in 1914. Same surname and town as Herbert Kohlmann, Thomas's father, and of an age to be his father, but nothing links him to the family. He is shown as a suspected relative only.
people.story: In 1921 the Bautzen address book lists "Kohlmann, Alwin, Fleischergeselle" (journeyman butcher) at Holzmarkt 27, in the rear building, first floor.[^anc-bautzen-1921-kohlmann] In 1924 he is a butcher (Fleischer) at Holzmarkt 27, ground floor.[^anc-bautzen-1924-kohlmann] From 1925 he lives at Schäfferstraße 6, and he is there in every book seen up to 1938.[^anc-bautzen-1925-kohlmann][^slub-bautzen-1928][^anc-bautzen-1935-kohlmann][^slub-bautzen-1938] He is the only Alwin Kohlmann in each book, and there is no second, younger Kohlmann butcher. Thomas Kohlmann's father was Herbert Kohlmann, who married Christa Eifler in Bautzen in 1952. This Alwin, born in 1883, could belong to Herbert's parents' generation, but nothing found so far links him to Herbert or to the family. (An older idea that Thomas's father was called Alvin, and might be this Alwin, came from a mix-up with Christa's father Alwin Eifler and is closed.) The Bautzen death name index for 1972 lists "Kohlmann, Ernst Alwin", who died on 27 February 1972, death register number 185.[^findbuch-death-index-1972-kohlmann] He is the only Alwin Kohlmann in the Bautzen death indexes from 1946 to 1979, so he is probably the butcher, but the index gives no age or address. The register entry itself would give his birth and next of kin.[^findbuch-death-indexes-1946-1972] His death entry in the Bautzen register for 1972 settles who he was: Ernst Alwin Kohlmann of Schäfferstraße 6, the same house as in the address books, died on 27 February 1972. He was born on 21 September 1883 at Kötzschau, a hamlet near Lawalde in Kreis Löbau, and was married to Marie Ida Kohlmann née Jurack; the marriage was registered at Malschwitz in 1914.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Marie Ida died in Bautzen less than a year later, on 20 January 1973.[^findbuch-death-indexes-1946-1972] The entry does not name his parents or any children. A second Kohlmann from the same village died in Bautzen in 1980: Ernestine Hedwig Kissal née Kohlmann, born on 15 September 1897 at Kleindehsa, the village that Kötzschau belongs to. She married Ernst Hermann Kissal at Lawalde in 1926 and lived at Mättigstraße 17.[^findbuch-death-register-1980-40] She was probably Alwin's younger sister, which would make this Bautzen Kohlmann family one from the Lawalde parish near Löbau.

openQuestions.question: Was he Herbert Kohlmann's father? The 1952 marriage entry (Standesamt Bautzen) names Herbert's parents and would show whether this family is connected.
Who were his parents? His 1914 marriage entry (Malschwitz Nr. 9/1914) and his 1883 birth entry (Lawalde Nr. 71/1883) name them.
Was Ernestine Hedwig Kissal née Kohlmann (1897 to 1980) his sister? Her 1926 Lawalde marriage entry (Nr. 4/1926) names her parents.

people.disambiguator: tax official in Döbeln, a lead for Brigitte's family
people.summary: Max Woltmann, a tax official, was the only Woltmann in the Döbeln address books of 1925 and 1939, at the same house both times. Rita was born a Woltmann in Döbeln in 1956, so he may be Brigitte's father or another close relative. Not proven.
people.story: The Döbeln address book for 1925 lists "Woltmann Max, Steuerassist." (tax assistant) at Kleinbauchlitzer Straße 20. He is the only Woltmann in the book.[^slub-doebeln-1925] In 1939 the book lists "Woltmann, Max, Steuersekretär" (tax secretary) at Grimmaische Straße 20, again the only Woltmann.[^slub-doebeln-1939] The 1939 book heads Grimmaische Straße "vorher Kleinbauchlitzer Straße" (formerly Kleinbauchlitzer Straße), so this is the same house: he lived at No. 20 from at least 1925 to 1939 and was promoted from assistant to secretary.[^slub-doebeln-1939] There was no Woltmann in Döbeln in 1900-01, so he came to the town after 1900.[^slub-doebeln-1900] Rita was born in Döbeln in 1956 with her mother Brigitte's surname, Woltmann.[^family-testimony] With so rare a name, Max is probably Brigitte's father or grandfather, but no record seen so far links them. Brigitte's birth entry would settle it. Ancestry's copies of the same two books show the same entries; Ancestry has no birth, marriage or death record for him, and none for Brigitte.[^anc-doebeln-1925][^anc-doebeln-1939]

facts.label: A Max Woltmann in the First World War
facts.value: A Sergeant Max Woltmann of Mittweida, district Rochlitz, Infantry Regiment 139, was wounded in the first weeks of the war (casualty list of 9 October 1914). Mittweida is 20 km from Döbeln and had other Woltmanns; he may be the later Döbeln tax official, but nothing proves it.

occupations.title: Sattlermeister (master saddler); saddlery and upholstery shop, firm name Weickert & Eifler

facts.label: Marriage
facts.value: Married Marie Martha Kuschel, a seamstress, in Bautzen on 7 September 1918 (Standesamt Bautzen Nr. 135/1918). The marriage index calls him a saddler and "z. Zt. Kanonier d. Res., z. Zt. im Felde": a reserve gunner, away at the front, so he married while on leave in the last months of the First World War.

facts.label: Same age as his partner
facts.value: Born 2 December 1892, eight weeks after Alwin Eifler (7 October 1892). The two founders of the firm were the same age.

facts.label: Not family
facts.value: Bruno Weickert was Alwin Eifler's business partner, not a relative. He is on the map as a business associate and not on the tree.

facts.label: Master saddler, 1920
facts.value: Passed his master saddler's examination at Bautzen on 21 April 1920, one of five candidates. The paper noted that all five had served in the war and some had not worked at their trade for four years, yet every piece was done with care.

facts.label: Partner, 1922 to 1923
facts.value: Co-founder with Alwin Eifler of the Stahldrahtmatratzenfabrik Weickert & Eifler, registered as a partnership founded on 11 October 1922 (Bautzen commercial register Blatt 885). He left in January 1923, and Alwin carried on alone under the old name.

media.caption: Bautzen death register 1956, Nr. 225: Max Bruno Weickert, master saddler, Fischergasse 31, born 2 December 1892 in Großschönau, died 26 March 1956; married Marie Martha née Kuschel, Bautzen 7 Sept 1918 Nr. 135. Archivverbund Bautzen 61003 vol 86 p226, CC BY 4.0.
media.alt: Typed civil death entry number 225 of 1956 from Bautzen, highlighted: Max Bruno Weickert, master saddler, Fischergasse 31.

media.caption: Bautzener Nachrichten, 23 April 1920: Bruno Weickert among the five saddlers who passed the master's examination on 21 April. SLUB Dresden.
media.alt: Highlighted news item about the saddlers' master examination.

openQuestions.question: His parents: the 1918 marriage entry (Bautzen Nr. 135/1918, not online) names them. Karl Gottlieb Weickert, shoemaker at Neusalzaer Straße 20, may be his father.
When and why he left the firm: the Handelsregister file at the Archivverbund Bautzen.

people.summary: Master saddler and co-founder of Weickert & Eifler with Alwin Eifler. Not family.
people.story: Max Bruno Weickert, master saddler, was the Weickert of Weickert & Eifler. Born on 2 December 1892 in Großschönau near Zittau, he ran the saddlery and upholstery shop at Löbauer Straße 10 that carried the firm's name in 1921. By 1928 Alwin Eifler was the sole owner. Bruno died at home, Fischergasse 31 in Bautzen, on 26 March 1956.[^findbuch-death-register-1956-225][^anc-bautzen-1921]

people.disambiguator: Alwin's brother, from the family chart
people.summary: Brother of Alwin Eifler, named on the 2007 family chart. Dates and places are not yet known.
people.story: The 2007 family chart names Max as a brother of Alwin Eifler (1892 to 1968).[^ahnentafel-2007] Nothing more is known yet: not the dates, not where he lived. On this tree he is drawn as a child of Ernst Eifler, the Sohland farmer who was probably Alwin's father; that link is not proven, so the line is dashed. A Max Eifler lived in Bautzen at Paulistraße 32 and is listed right under Alwin in the 1928 address book, but his 1978 death entry shows he was Max Oswald Eifler, born on 2 March 1892 at Oberrennersdorf, seven months before Alwin and in another village, so he cannot be Alwin's full brother.[^findbuch-death-register-1978-704]

openQuestions.question: When and where was Max born? Alwin's Sohland birth entry (1892) and the Sohland church books would give the parents and the other children.
Max Oswald Eifler of Paulistraße 32 (1892 to 1978) is not this Max. Was he a cousin?

people.summary: Alwin Eifler's elder sister, the first child of Ernst Gustav Eifler and Johanna Christiane Kahden. Born 1890 in Sohland, died 1932.
people.story: Martha Maria Eifler was born on 10 February 1890 at half past one in the afternoon in the house Äußerst Mittelsohland Nr. 250, Sohland an der Spree, and baptised on 23 February. She was the first child of the baker Ernst Gustav Eifler and Johanna Christiane née Kahden, two and a half years older than her brother Alwin. Her godparents were a weaver from Wehrsdorf and two unmarried women from Mittelsohland and Wehrsdorf. A note added in the margin of the church book gives her death: 2 November 1932, when she was 42.[^sohland-kb-1890] The 2007 family chart names her as Alwin's sister.[^ahnentafel-2007]

openQuestions.question: Did Martha marry, and where did she die in 1932?

people.disambiguator: Richard's sister, from the family chart
people.summary: Richard Becker's sister, named in a handwritten note on the 2007 family chart, with the address Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden. Her married surname is perhaps Wettlitz.
people.story: The 2007 family chart records two sisters of Richard Becker, and a handwritten note names one of them as Marie, with a married surname that seems to read Wettlitz (or Wettlich, or Wettnitz), at Rothermundtstraße 5 in Dresden, Richard's own address.[^ahnentafel-2007] She was probably born in Herzberg on the Black Elster, like Richard, between about 1870 and 1885, but no record of her has been found yet. The Dresden house registers for Rothermundtstraße 5 in 1938 and 1943 list nobody under a W name, so she may have lived there earlier or later.[^slub-dresden-1938] She is drawn beside Richard with a dashed line because no record yet proves the link.

openQuestions.question: What was her married name? The Dresden address books from 1925 to 1943 and the Herzberg church books are the next places to look.

people.summary: The 2007 family chart records that Richard Becker had two sisters. This is the second one; her name is not on the page the family holds.
people.story: The 2007 family chart records two sisters of Richard Becker. One is Marie; the other is not named on page 1, the only page the family has.[^ahnentafel-2007] Page 2 of the chart may name her.

openQuestions.question: What was her name? Page 2 of the 2007 chart, or the Herzberg church books, would tell.

facts.label: Juracks of Briesing in the First World War
facts.value: The Saxon casualty lists name two men from her village: Unteroffizier Ernst Jurack of Briesing, killed in 1915, and Gustav Jurack of Briesing, born on 23 January, missing in 1917, then a prisoner of war, and back home by July 1918. Same surname, same small village; whether they were her brothers or cousins is not known.

media.caption: Saxon casualty list Nr. 200, 30 September 1915: Unteroffizier Ernst Jurack of Briesing, Bautzen, killed. Index: Verein für Computergenealogie.
media.alt: Highlighted line in a printed casualty list.

people.disambiguator: wife of Alwin Kohlmann the butcher
people.summary: Wife of Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a Bautzen butcher who is one of the leads for Herbert Kohlmann's family. Born at Briesing in 1887, married at Malschwitz in 1914, died in Bautzen in 1973. Not proven to be family.
people.story: Marie Ida Jurack was born on 5 February 1887 at Briesing near Malschwitz, north of Bautzen, and married Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, a butcher, at Malschwitz in 1914 (register Nr. 9/1914). She was his widow when he died in February 1972 and died herself on 20 January 1973 in Bautzen, living at Am Stadtwall 1.[^findbuch-death-register-1973-55][^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Briesing was a Sorbian village: when Arnošt Muka counted the villages in 1884 and 1885, 176 of its 183 people were Sorbs, and Jurack is a Sorbian surname (from Jurij, George).[^wikipedia-briesing] Whether her own family spoke Sorbian at home is not yet known. Her husband is one of the leads being checked for Herbert Kohlmann's family. Nothing links either of them to the family, so she is shown as a suspected relative only, not as an ancestor.

openQuestions.question: Did she and Alwin have children? The Malschwitz marriage entry (1914) gives both sets of parents, and Bautzen births from 1914 would show any children.

facts.label: Marriage
facts.value: Married Ernst Hermann Kissal, registered at Lawalde, Kreis Löbau, Nr. 4/1926. He was still living when she died in 1980.

people.summary: Born at Kleindehsa in 1897, the village Kötzschau belongs to, where Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born in 1883. Probably his sister; not proven.
people.story: Ernestine Hedwig Kohlmann was born on 15 September 1897 at Kleindehsa, Kreis Löbau. She married Ernst Hermann Kissal at Lawalde in 1926 (Nr. 4/1926) and died in Bautzen on 14 January 1980, living at Mättigstraße 17; her husband was still alive.[^findbuch-death-register-1980-40] Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born in 1883 at Kötzschau, a hamlet of Kleindehsa, and registered at the same office, Lawalde.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] Same surname, same village, fourteen years apart: she was probably his sister, but no record seen yet names their parents.

openQuestions.question: Who were her parents? The Lawalde marriage entry of 1926 (Nr. 4) would name them, and so would answer whether she was Alwin's sister.

people.summary: Richter (village judge) of Kötzschau, father of Gottfried Kohlmann, who bought the Kleindehsa inn in 1787.
people.story: In 1787 Gottfried Kohlmann, "son of the judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötschau", bought the Kretscham at Kleindehsa.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] The village judge (Richter) presided over the village court and spoke for the village to the manor. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

facts.label: A dispute over firewood, 1824 to 1830
facts.value: The Saxon State Archives keep a court file of 1824 to 1830 from the Upper Lusatian government: "Gottfried Kohlmann, Kleindehsa, against Gottlob Randig and others, over the demanded yearly delivery of a cord of wood from the village forest". An older file of 1807 to 1809 from the Kleindehsa manor court concerns Johann George Manitz and others of Kötzschau against a Christian Kohlmann who had refused part of his labour service for the manor.

people.summary: Son of the village judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötzschau. In 1787 he bought the Kretscham, the village inn of Kleindehsa, for 600 Taler; the family kept it for about 150 years.
people.story: In 1787 Gottfried Kohlmann, son of the judge Johann Kohlmann of Kötzschau, bought the Kretschamgut, the village inn with its farm, from the widow of an appeal court councillor, von Heldreich, for 600 Taler. From then on the inn stayed in the Kohlmann family for 150 years.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] Forty years earlier, in 1748 and 1749, the manor had built the inn new and sold it to an innkeeper who had to hand over the tongue of every ox he slaughtered and pour only Löbau beer. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

facts.label: Butcher and innkeeper, 1856
facts.value: In February 1856 the Dresdner Journal reported that thieves had several times taken cattle hides hung up to dry in the loft of the slaughterhouse of "Fleischer und Schenkwirth J. T. Kohlmann" in Kleindehsa: Johann Traugott Kohlmann kept the inn and was the village butcher too.

people.story: The village chronicle lists Johann Traugott Kohlmann as the owner of the Kretscham from 1809.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

facts.label: The Kretscham owner, 1874 to 1885
facts.value: In December 1874 "Kretschamsbesitzer Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann in Kleindehsa" was named to a district commission, and in March 1885 "Ernst Kohlmann" advertised cows for sale "im Kretscham zu Kleindehsa". In April 1889 the court sold the Kretscham from the estate of Christiane Elisabeth, widow Kohlmann, née Kriegel. So the innkeeper Ernst and Karl Friedrich Ernst, husband of Christiane Elisabeth Kriegel, were very probably the same man, who died before 1889.

media.caption: Bautzener Nachrichten, 14 March 1885: young cows for sale in the Kretscham at Kleindehsa, Ernst Kohlmann. SLUB Dresden, public domain.
media.alt: Small Gothic advertisement, highlighted.

people.disambiguator: owner of the Kleindehsa inn from 1860
people.summary: Owner of the Kretscham at Kleindehsa from 1860; his widow held it in 1888.
people.story: The village chronicle lists Ernst Kohlmann as the owner of the Kretscham from 1860, and his widow in 1888.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns. He may be the Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann whom another researcher's tree names as the father of Maria Alwine Kohlmann, born at Kleindehsa in 1868; that is not proven.[^anc-tree-kirchhoff]

facts.label: Master butcher and cattle dealer, 1913
facts.value: In April 1913 the paper called him "Fleischermeister und Viehhändler Reinhold Kohlmann in Kleindehsa" (master butcher and cattle dealer). His eldest son, aged 19, was badly hurt that month when his cart overturned on the steep road from the Neue Schenke down to Obercunewalde; he was found unconscious with a fractured skull.

facts.label: A second Reinhold, 1925
facts.value: In November 1925 a "Reinhold Kohlmann-Kleindehsa" passed the master butcher's examination, probably his son of the same name.

facts.label: Kohlmann's Gasthof, 1926 to 1931
facts.value: Bus timetables of 1926 have a stop called "Kleindehsa, Kohlmanns Gasthof". On 2 May 1931 the inn served supper to men from a Nazi party training course held at the Kleindehsa manor by its owner, Hans von Tschammer und Osten; a court report on a brawl later that night names the "Gasthaus von Kohlmann" only as the place of the meal.

media.caption: Bautzener Nachrichten, 24 April 1913: the eldest son of the master butcher and cattle dealer Reinhold Kohlmann of Kleindehsa badly hurt in a cart accident. SLUB Dresden.
media.alt: Highlighted local news item.

people.disambiguator: took over the Kleindehsa inn in 1885
people.summary: Took over the inn at Kleindehsa in 1885, according to the village chronicle.
people.story: The village chronicle says Karl August Reinhold Kohlmann took over the inn in 1885.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] Alwin Kohlmann the butcher was born two years earlier, in 1883, at Kötzschau, a hamlet of the same village.[^findbuch-death-register-1972-185] The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

openQuestions.question: Was he the father of Alwin Kohlmann (born 1883 at Kötzschau) and of Ernestine Hedwig (born 1897 at Kleindehsa)? Alwin's Lawalde birth entry, 1883 Nr. 71, names his parents.

people.disambiguator: owner of the Kleindehsa inn after 1927
people.summary: Became owner of the Kretscham some years after 1927; after his death his brother Ernst and a daughter kept it until 1959.
people.story: In 1927 a hall was opened on the south side of the Kretscham. Some years later Gustav Kohlmann became the owner, and after his death his brother Ernst and his daughter held it until 1959.[^lawalde-chronik-kleindehsa] From 1958 the Senftenberg brown coal combine ran a holiday camp in a side wing, and after 1959 the whole inn passed to the combine. The Kretscham burned down on the evening of 29 January 1997 and was pulled down. The village chronicle gives only the year each owner took over; it does not say how they were related to one another, and no record yet links them to the Bautzen Kohlmanns.

openQuestions.question: Gustav's brother Ernst: could he be Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, the Bautzen butcher? Nothing links them yet.

facts.value: In December 1874 "Kretschamsbesitzer Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann in Kleindehsa" was named to a district commission, and in March 1885 "Ernst Kohlmann" advertised cows for sale "im Kretscham zu Kleindehsa". In April 1889 the court sold the Kretscham from the estate of Christiane Elisabeth, widow Kohlmann, née Kriegel. So the innkeeper Ernst and Karl Friedrich Ernst, husband of Christiane Elisabeth Kriegel, were very probably the same man, who died before 1889.

Was the Bautzen butcher Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, born at Kötzschau in 1883, one of his children?

people.disambiguator: of Kleindehsa, father of Maria Alwine
people.summary: Named in another researcher's tree as the father of Maria Alwine Kohlmann of Kleindehsa (born 1868). Possibly the innkeeper Ernst Kohlmann.
people.story: Another researcher's Ancestry tree names Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann and Christiane Elisabeth Kriegel (born 1848) as the parents of Maria Alwine Kohlmann, born at Kleindehsa in 1868.[^anc-tree-kirchhoff] He may be the Ernst Kohlmann who owned the village inn from 1860 and whose widow held it in 1888, but nothing proves they are the same man. If he is, he would have died before 1888.

facts.label: The Kretscham sold, 1889
facts.value: By April 1889 she had died as the widow of Kohlmann. To divide her estate the Löbau court auctioned the Kretscham at Kleindehsa (7.9 hectares, insured for 12,070 marks, without its inventory) and a pasture and spruce wood at Großdehsa, on 29 April 1889.

media.caption: Bautzener Nachrichten, 15 April 1889: court sale of the Kretscham at Kleindehsa from the estate of Christiane Elisabeth, widow Kohlmann, née Kriegel. SLUB Dresden, public domain.
media.alt: Highlighted court notice.

people.summary: Born 1848; named in another researcher's tree as the mother of Maria Alwine Kohlmann.
people.story: Another researcher's Ancestry tree gives Christiane Elisabeth Kriegel, born in 1848, as the wife of Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann and the mother of Maria Alwine Kohlmann.[^anc-tree-kirchhoff]

people.summary: Born and died at Kleindehsa (1868 to 1900); married Fritz Kirchhoff at Lawalde in 1891.
people.story: Another researcher's Ancestry tree says Maria Alwine Kohlmann was born at Kleindehsa on 23 May 1868, married Fritz Wilhelm Otto Hermann Kirchhoff (1853 to 1937) at Lawalde on 6 July 1891, had a son, Ernst Otto Fritz Kirchhoff (1893 to 1962), born at Kleindehsa on 24 January 1893, and died at Kleindehsa on 30 March 1900, aged 31.[^anc-tree-kirchhoff] Her middle name, Alwine, and her father's name, Ernst, are the two names of the Bautzen butcher Ernst Alwin Kohlmann, born nearby in 1883. That could point to one family, but nothing links them yet.

people.disambiguator: of Kleindehsa, married Kutschke at Cunnewalde
people.summary: Born at Kleindehsa; married Johann Carl Traugott Kutschke and died at Cunnewalde. Her son was born there in 1857.
people.story: Another researcher's Ancestry tree says Johanne Sophie Helene Kohlmann was born at Kleindehsa, married Johann Carl Traugott Kutschke and died at Cunnewalde, a village about 8 km to the west. Their son Karl Friedrich Ernst Kutschke was born at Cunnewalde on 31 July 1857.[^anc-tree-augsten] The boy shares all three given names with Karl Friedrich Ernst Kohlmann of Kleindehsa, which might mean he was named after an uncle, but the tree gives no dates for her and no parents.

people.disambiguator: of Kleindehsa, soldier, prisoner of war 1918 to 1919
people.summary: A Kleindehsa Kohlmann born in 1897 who went missing with Infantry Regiment 107 in 1918 and turned out to be a prisoner of war.
people.story: Hermann Kohlmann was born at Kleindehsa on 11 December 1897. He served with the Saxon Infantry Regiment 107. The casualty list of 10 January 1919 reported him missing; a correction of 26 August 1919 says he had been taken prisoner.[^vl-kohlmann-hermann-1919] He was born three months after Ernestine Hedwig Kohlmann of the same village, so the two cannot have been brother and sister; he may have been a cousin, perhaps of the innkeeping family. Another Kleindehsa man, Paul Kohlmann, was wounded twice in 1916.

media.caption: Saxon casualty list Nr. 568, 10 January 1919: "Kohlmann, Hermann, 11. 12. 97 Kleindehsa, Löbau, vermißt". Index: Verein für Computergenealogie.
media.alt: Highlighted line in a printed casualty list.

openQuestions.question: Who were his parents, and when did he come home?
